current_role: U.S. Secretary of Labor (acting from April 2026; confirmed September 30, 2026)
summary: Keith Sonderling, a Florida labor and employment lawyer, joined Trump's Labor Department in 2017 and led its Wage and Hour Division, then served as an EEOC commissioner (2020–2024), where he focused on AI in hiring. Confirmed as Deputy Secretary of Labor in March 2025, he became acting secretary when Lori Chavez-DeRemer resigned in April 2026 and was confirmed as the 31st Secretary of Labor on September 30, 2026, by a 47–41 vote.
